articles.title: Is CoreWeave Stock a Buy After Its Latest Earnings?
articles.summary: CoreWeave delivered impressive Q3 earnings with 168% YoY revenue growth to $3.7B and a $132.5B customer backlog, but still reported a $709M net loss. While the company is executing well and raising guidance, it faces challenges converting growth into profits due to massive capital investments in infrastructure and high financing costs. The stock is viewed as a speculative opportunity after its recent sell-off, but remains risky for conservative investors until profitability improves.

articles.title: 5 Dividend Stocks With High Yields That Are Safer Than You Might Think
articles.summary: The article examines five high-yield dividend stocks that appear riskier than they actually are. Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb face normal pharmaceutical industry headwinds from patent expirations but maintain sustainable dividends through strong cash flows. REITs Realty Income and W.P. Carey are pressured by rising interest rates, but historical market adjustments should protect profitability. Hormel Foods, despite slow turnaround progress, has strong financials and backing from the Hormel Foundation, making its dividend safer than its yield suggests.

articles.title: Apple's Market Value Grew From $350 Billion to $4 Trillion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO. Here's What That Growth Curve Means for Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus
articles.summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO after 15 years, during which the company's market value grew from $350 billion to $4.6 trillion. While new CEO John Ternus is unlikely to match Cook's exceptional returns, Apple remains well-positioned for growth through popular products like the iPhone 17 and new innovations like the iPhone Duo foldable smartphone, along with its strong services segment and shareholder capital returns.

articles.title: Accenture vs. Adobe: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Accenture and Adobe as investment options for 2027. Accenture is a global consulting powerhouse serving 75% of Fortune Global 500 companies with steady 6.5% revenue growth, while Adobe dominates creative software with stronger 12% revenue growth and higher profit margins. Despite Adobe facing management turmoil and regulatory challenges, its cheaper forward P/E ratio and better growth-to-valuation mix make it the recommended choice for 2027.

articles.title: Most AI Stocks Need Perfect Conditions to Win. This One Doesn't.
articles.summary: Alphabet stands out among AI stocks due to its diversified revenue streams from artificial intelligence. The company is profiting from AI through Google Cloud (which more than doubled revenue), custom TPU chip sales to external customers, and AI-enhanced Search features. With multiple ways to generate AI revenue, Alphabet doesn't need every aspect of the AI boom to succeed perfectly to remain highly profitable.

articles.title: AT&T vs. Verizon: Which Telecom Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: AT&T and Verizon are compared as investment options for 2027, with both trading at similar valuations. AT&T has refocused on wireless and fiber broadband after divesting entertainment assets, while Verizon maintains the largest wireless subscriber base and is expanding fiber through acquisitions. The article recommends Verizon as the better choice due to its 20-year streak of consecutive dividend increases, compared to AT&T's dividend freeze since 2022.

articles.title: Alibaba vs. Uber Technologies: Which Tech Platform Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Alibaba and Uber Technologies as investment options for 2027. Alibaba trades at a lower valuation multiple (P/E 20.96) and focuses on e-commerce and AI cloud services in China, but faces regulatory risks and intense domestic competition. Uber trades at a higher multiple (P/E 41.33) with strong profitability and global growth prospects, but faces regulatory challenges around driver classification. The analyst recommends Uber as the better buy for 2027, citing lower volatility compared to Alibaba's exposure to Chinese market uncertainties and AI volatility.

articles.title: Credo Technology Group vs. Marvell Technology: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares two semiconductor companies competing in the AI infrastructure market. Credo Technology Group demonstrates explosive 165% revenue growth with strong profitability margins and minimal debt, but faces customer concentration risk. Marvell Technology offers greater scale at $9.5 billion in revenue with 30.6% growth and a diversified portfolio, but carries higher valuation multiples. The analyst concludes Credo is the better buy for 2027 based on superior growth, profitability, and valuation metrics.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk vs. Pfizer: Does a Weight Loss or Cancer Focused Pharma Stock Make a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Novo Nordisk and Pfizer as investment choices for 2027. Novo Nordisk dominates the high-growth obesity and diabetes treatment markets with blockbuster drugs like Wegovy and Ozempic, but faces pricing pressures and competition from rivals like Eli Lilly. Pfizer offers a diversified portfolio, stronger cash position ($14.3B vs $6.8B), and cheaper valuation, making it the better turnaround bet despite slower growth. Both companies face headwinds from pricing pressures and competitive threats.

articles.title: Axsome Therapeutics vs. Moderna: Which Biotech Innovator Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: Axsome Therapeutics and Moderna represent different biotech investment profiles. Axsome shows strong 54% revenue growth with three marketed drugs and a narrowing path to profitability, trading at conservative valuations (41x forward P/E). Moderna, despite its revolutionary mRNA platform, faces declining COVID vaccine demand and significant losses ($2.8B net loss on $2.5B revenue), trading at a premium 249x forward P/E. The article recommends Axsome as the better 2027 buy due to superior valuation and near-term revenue visibility, while acknowledging Moderna's long-term potential.

articles.title: Warren Buffett Said This 1 Mistake Cost Berkshire About $10 Billion. Here’s How Investors Can Avoid It.
articles.summary: Warren Buffett revealed that his reluctance to pay a slightly higher price for Walmart shares cost Berkshire Hathaway approximately $10 billion. Instead of anchoring to an initial target price of $23 per share, Buffett waited for a pullback that never came, missing significant gains. The article provides three strategies to avoid this mistake: determine a stock's value before looking at price, set purchases in advance through staged buying, and weigh small premiums against expected upside.

articles.title: 3 Consumer Compounders That Fit Warren Buffett's Playbook. I'd Hold Them Forever.
articles.summary: The article identifies Coca-Cola, Procter & Gamble, and Kimberly-Clark as consumer staple companies that align with Warren Buffett's investment philosophy of buying and holding quality businesses with strong pricing power, steady cash flow, and consistent dividend growth. All three are Dividend Kings with reliable earnings despite challenging consumer markets, though valuations and risk profiles vary.

articles.title: Think Nvidia Stock Is a Bargain? 6 Reasons the Face of the AI Build-Out Can Plunge Another 50% Following Jensen Huang's Resignation.
articles.summary: Following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal misconduct allegations, Nvidia stock has fallen 32% from its peak. The article outlines six major risks that could drive the stock down another 50%: loss of company identity without Huang, potential slowdown in data center expansion due to Democratic governors, aggressive Fed rate hikes driven by AI-related inflation, warning signs in bond markets for hyperscalers, historical precedent of AI bubble-bursting events, and unsustainable premium valuations similar to the dot-com era.

articles.title: Opinion: Buy This Growth Stock to Beat the S&P 500 in 2027
articles.summary: DigitalOcean, an AI cloud services provider, has surged 65% in 2026 compared to the S&P 500's 10% return. The company is experiencing explosive demand for its AI Native Cloud platform, with AI customer revenue growing 288% and token volume increasing tenfold in Q3 2026. Management forecasts over 60% revenue growth for 2027, and the stock's valuation has become more attractive following a recent correction, positioning it to potentially outperform the broader market again next year.

articles.title: Jamie Dimon Just Said 5 Words Blocking Outside AI Agents From JPMorgan Accounts: "You Don't Want Rogue Agents." Here's Why That Security Stance Matters for JPM and Its Tech Rivals.
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned against allowing third-party AI agents like Meta's Muse to access customer accounts, citing security and regulatory risks including potential unauthorized transactions and compliance violations. United Airlines similarly announced restrictions on third-party AI agents for bookings, signaling that heavily regulated industries are taking a cautious stance on agentic AI integration.

articles.title: 4 Dividend Stocks Yielding 4% or More to Buy Before the End of November
articles.summary: The article recommends four dividend stocks with yields of 4% or higher: Realty Income (5.4% yield), Federal Realty (4% yield), PepsiCo (4.1% yield), and Hormel Foods (5.2% yield). The two REITs are positioned as industry leaders with complementary portfolios, while the consumer staples companies face temporary headwinds but remain well-run businesses with strong dividend histories.

articles.title: China Eastern Airlines Fechou 23 Contratos de Compra e Apresentou Inovações na 9ª CIIE
articles.summary: China Eastern Airlines (CEAir) signed 23 procurement agreements worth $540 million with international suppliers at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The airline secured contracts for aircraft engines, aviation materials, and cabin modernization services. CEAir also showcased innovations including an autonomous electric baggage tractor and modular aluminum hangar construction technology.

articles.title: China Eastern Airlines firma 23 accordi di approvvigionamento e svela le ultime innovazioni alla 9ª edizione della CIIE
articles.summary: China Eastern Airlines signed 23 procurement agreements worth $540 million with international suppliers at the 9th China International Import Expo. The airline secured deals for aircraft engines, aviation materials, jet fuel, and catering services, while showcasing innovations including autonomous baggage tractors and modular hangar construction to enhance operational efficiency and sustainability.

articles.title: China Eastern Airlines unterzeichnet 23 Beschaffungsverträge und präsentiert auf der 9. CIIE seine neuesten Innovationen
articles.summary: China Eastern Airlines signed 23 procurement contracts worth $540 million with international suppliers at the 9th China International Import Expo. The agreements cover aircraft engines, aviation materials, jet fuel, and catering services. Notable contracts include LEAP engines from CFM International, cabin modernization with Panasonic Avionics and Boeing, and catering services from SATS. CEAir also showcased innovations including an autonomous electric baggage tractor and modular aluminum hangars.

articles.title: Tariffs Pushed Prices Up. Why Retail and Industrial Investors Shouldn't Expect a Quick Reversal
articles.summary: U.S. tariff policy uncertainty is causing sticky price increases across supply chains that are unlikely to reverse quickly. Companies like Caterpillar and PepsiCo are facing significant tariff costs and broader inflation, and are reluctant to roll back price increases due to margin protection concerns and uncertainty about future tariff implementation. Even if tariffs are reduced, companies have little incentive to lower prices, and supply chain adjustments often result in permanently higher costs.

articles.title: Micron Technology vs. Qualcomm: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Micron Technology and Qualcomm as semiconductor investment options for 2027. Micron has experienced explosive revenue growth (256% YoY) driven by AI data center demand but faces volatility tied to memory pricing. Qualcomm's smartphone business has stalled but is diversifying into data centers and automotive. The author recommends Qualcomm as the safer long-term choice, citing its less cyclical business model and growth potential in existing data center spending, while warning that Micron's profitability is too dependent on memory price fluctuations.

articles.title: Is Apple Stock a Buy Right Now?
articles.summary: Apple stock has hit new all-time highs, trading 31% higher this year and outperforming other Magnificent Seven stocks. Despite a rich valuation of 40x trailing earnings, the article argues Apple remains a buy due to strong fundamentals including double-digit revenue growth, expanding margins above 20%, and successful price increases across products and services like the new iPhone Duo and Apple TV+.

articles.title: Chewy vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Chewy and Shopify as investment options through 2027. Chewy, a pet e-commerce specialist with a strong Autoship subscription model, trades at a more affordable valuation (P/E 29.2x) with steady 7% projected growth. Shopify, a merchant platform growing at 32.5% with superior margins, commands a premium valuation (P/E 78.7x) but faces higher execution risk. The author recommends Chewy as the better value for long-term investors despite Shopify's stronger growth trajectory.

articles.title: Advisor Insights — Brought to You By The Motley Fool
articles.summary: Markets faced a turbulent week with strong jobs data and hot inflation pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, increasing odds of a December rate hike. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid personal conduct allegations, causing the stock to plunge 14% intraday before recovering to close down 4%. The article advises advisors to audit client floating-rate debt, match bond duration to timelines, and separate leadership changes from business fundamentals.

articles.title: Advance Auto Parts vs. Airbnb: Is a Retail Rebound or Travel Giant Stock the Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Advance Auto Parts and Airbnb as investment options for 2027. Advance Auto Parts, a brick-and-mortar automotive retailer, faces challenges with declining sales, high debt (2.4x debt-to-equity), and negative free cash flow, though it's attempting a turnaround. Airbnb, an asset-light travel marketplace, demonstrates strong growth (16.9% revenue increase), healthy financials (0.3x debt-to-equity, $4.6B free cash flow), and expanding international markets. The analyst recommends Airbnb for 2027, viewing Advance Auto Parts as a 'prove it' year turnaround story.

articles.title: Walmart, Target, and Nvidia Headline a Pivotal Week for Q3 Earnings
articles.summary: As Q3 earnings season wraps up, the S&P 500 shows strong overall performance with earnings up 24.9% YoY on 13.7% higher revenues. Walmart faces valuation pressures despite defensive positioning, while Target has shown impressive momentum. Nvidia's upcoming earnings will conclude the Magnificent Seven reporting cycle. Retail sector results are mixed, with e-commerce and restaurant operators showing weaker revenue beats compared to historical averages.

articles.title: Why Intel Stock Slumped Today
articles.summary: Intel stock fell nearly 3% on Friday amid concerns about leadership changes at Nvidia. The decline reflects uncertainty about Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress replacing Jensen Huang, and potential impacts on Nvidia's $13 billion Intel shareholding and their collaborative x86 CPU development. Investors are cautious until the situation clarifies.

articles.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 13: Cerebras Surges Over 11% on Record Q3 Revenue and Raised 2026 Guidance
articles.summary: Cerebras Systems surged 11.22% after reporting record Q3 revenue of $210.8 million (55% YoY growth) and raising 2026 guidance. The company added Microsoft as a customer alongside Oracle and Amazon. The stock rally was also supported by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, potentially opening market share opportunities for Cerebras.

articles.title: Nov. 25 Could Be a Huge Day for the Stock Market
articles.summary: Recent inflation reports showing higher-than-expected CPI and PPI readings have increased the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December from 0% to over 12%. The final PCE inflation report on Nov. 25 will be crucial in determining whether the Fed implements a half-point hike. This matters significantly for AI-focused tech companies that are increasingly relying on debt to fund expensive data center projects, as higher rates would make these investments harder to justify.

articles.title: Top Stock Reports for Visa, ExxonMobil & Pfizer
articles.summary: Zacks analysts published research on 16 major stocks on November 13, 2026. Visa benefits from strong brand and digital growth but faces profitability pressures. ExxonMobil gains from low-cost production and expansion opportunities but faces commodity volatility risks. Pfizer underperforms peers due to patent expirations and subdued growth, though pipeline investments offer longer-term potential. Additional coverage includes U.S. Bancorp, Blackstone, Edwards Lifesciences, and others with mixed outlooks.

articles.title: Quick-Service Restaurant Market to Reach USD 1.87 Trillion by 2032 as Digital Ordering and Drive-Thru Access Expand - Mordor Intelligence
articles.summary: The global QSR market is projected to grow from USD 1.16 trillion in 2026 to USD 1.87 trillion by 2032, at an 8.18% CAGR. Growth is driven by digital ordering, drive-thru formats, and loyalty programs, with North America leading the market. Major operators are expanding through omnichannel strategies and technology integration to maintain competitive positioning.

articles.title: If You'd Invested $1,000 in ExxonMobil 1 Year Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Today
articles.summary: A $1,000 investment in ExxonMobil one year ago would be worth $1,432 today, driven by higher oil prices and stronger refining margins amid the Iran conflict. ExxonMobil's upstream earnings jumped 16% to $20.8 billion while downstream earnings surged 181% to $11.4 billion. The company is investing in cost-efficient assets to lower its breakeven cost to $35 by 2027 and $30 by 2030, positioning it to remain profitable even if oil prices decline.

articles.title: JPMorgan Stock Slid After Reports That Senate Democrats Plan a New Investigation Into Jamie Dimon's Bank Over Its Jeffrey Epstein Relationship. Here's Why That Political Risk Could Weigh on JPM Shares.
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase's stock declined following reports that Senate Democrats plan to investigate the bank's historical ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Epstein banked at JPMorgan from 1998-2013, with the bank processing over $1 billion in transactions and generating $8 million in fees. A former executive exchanged over 1,200 emails with Epstein despite red flags. While the bank settled a 2023 class action lawsuit for $290 million with no admission of wrongdoing, new investigations could lead to additional fines, regulatory orders, increased compliance costs, or reputational damage, potentially weighing on the stock in the near term.

articles.title: Can UNH's Optum Rx Sustain Profit Growth as Prescription Volumes Fall?
articles.summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum Rx segment increased operating earnings by 10.9% to $1.72 billion in Q3 2026 despite a 5.1% decline in adjusted prescriptions, driven by biosimilar adoption and operational efficiencies. However, membership losses and declining prescription volumes pose sustainability challenges for future growth. Specialty pharmacy volumes grew 2.6%, offering some offset to overall volume pressures.

articles.title: You Can Do Better Than Tesla: 3 Industrial Stocks With More Upside
articles.summary: The article argues that three industrial stocks—Caterpillar, Lockheed Martin, and GE Vernova—offer better investment opportunities than Tesla. These companies benefit from AI-driven electricity demand and defense spending, with record order backlogs stretching years into the future. Caterpillar's power generation revenue surged 75%, Lockheed Martin's backlog reached $292 billion, and GE Vernova's backlog hit $197 billion, while Tesla faces margin pressures and a softening EV market.

articles.title: Is Walmart (WMT) Stock Too Expensive to Buy Now?
articles.summary: Walmart's stock has surged significantly, gaining 73.5% in 2024, but is now richly valued with a price-to-sales ratio of 1.37 (above the five-year average of 0.85) and a forward P/E ratio of 38 (above the five-year average of 27). The author recommends waiting for a better entry price rather than buying at current levels, suggesting investors could achieve better returns if they wait for a potential pullback to around $100 per share.

articles.title: Why Is Morgan Stanley (MS) Up 3.9% Since Last Earnings Report?
articles.summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.03 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $2.83, with net revenues rising 11.6% year-over-year to $20.34 billion. The Wealth Management segment hit record revenues of $9.07 billion with $8.43 trillion in client assets, while Institutional Securities benefited from strong equity trading revenues. However, Investment Management faced headwinds with an 11.6% revenue decline due to performance fee pressure. The stock has gained 3.9% since the earnings report and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

articles.title: Chevron Eyes Biodiesel Growth With Iowa Facility Restart
articles.summary: Chevron Corporation plans to restart its Ralston, Iowa biodiesel facility, which has been idle since 2024, as market conditions improve. The facility has a capacity of nearly 42 million gallons annually and will benefit from a partnership with Landus Cooperative, which operates a nearby soybean-processing facility handling over 28 million bushels yearly. The restart will occur in phases with no specific date announced yet.

articles.title: Can APA's High-Quality Portfolio Fuel Cash Flow and Future Growth?
articles.summary: APA Corporation is leveraging stable production from the Permian Basin and Egypt while pursuing long-term offshore growth, particularly through the GranMorgu development in Suriname scheduled for mid-2028. The company exceeded Q3 U.S. oil production guidance and raised its 2026 outlook to 124,000 bpd. APA's stock has surged 99.5% over the past year, trading at a discount to industry averages with expected 78.3% year-over-year earnings growth.

articles.title: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold Starbucks Stock Post Q4 Earnings?
articles.summary: Starbucks reported mixed Q4 fiscal 2026 results with EPS beating estimates by 9.6% while revenues missed by 1.4%. The company projects fiscal 2027 EPS growth of ~18% supported by sales leverage and cost savings, but faces headwinds from China's licensing transition, higher product costs, and intensifying beverage competition. Analysts recommend a Hold rating, suggesting investors maintain positions while awaiting better entry points.

articles.title: CBRS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Strong Cloud Growth
articles.summary: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 13 cents per share, beating estimates, with revenues surging 70% year-over-year to $230.87 million. Cloud revenues soared 272% to $144.91 million driven by AI inference demand and higher pricing. The company secured partnerships with Oracle and Microsoft, raised 2026 revenue guidance to $940-$960 million, and expects to triple revenues in 2027 with expanding data center capacity.

articles.title: Wall Street Divided on S&P 500: Which ETFs Could Benefit in 2027?
articles.summary: Wall Street strategists are divided on the S&P 500's 2027 outlook. UBS forecasts the index reaching 8,900 (17.22% upside) driven by earnings growth, while Bank of America warns that crowded equity positioning, AI valuation risks, and potential outflows could limit gains. The divergence highlights key risks including elevated valuations, geopolitical uncertainty, and concentration in mega-cap tech stocks.

articles.title: Home Depot Pre-Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy or Stay Cautious?
articles.summary: Home Depot is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on November 17 with projected revenue growth of 3.3% to $42.7B and EPS growth of 3.5%. While the company benefits from strong Pro sales, digital expansion, and smaller home improvement projects, near-term challenges include weak housing turnover, margin pressures from tariffs and operating costs, and a premium valuation of 22.27X forward P/E.

articles.title: Moderna Issues Cost Outlook Amid Revenue Uncertainty, Stock Falls
articles.summary: Moderna outlined its growth strategy at its 2026 Analyst Day, highlighting oncology as a key long-term opportunity with intismeran autogene for melanoma treatment. However, shares fell 7% as the company projected $4 billion in 2027 cash costs and $4-$4.5 billion annually through 2030, while providing limited visibility into 2027 and longer-term revenue growth.

articles.title: Why Microsoft (MSFT) is a Top Growth Stock for the Long-Term
articles.summary: Zacks Premium offers Style Scores (Value, Growth, Momentum, and VGM) that work alongside the Zacks Rank to help investors identify stocks with the highest likelihood of outperformance. The Zacks Rank #1 stocks have averaged +23.7% annual returns since 1988. Microsoft is highlighted as a stock to watch with a #3 Hold rank and B VGM Score, showing strong growth prospects with 10.9% forecasted earnings growth.

articles.title: The Home Depot, Inc. (HD) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
articles.summary: Home Depot stock has gained 13% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500. The company shows solid fundamentals with consistent earnings and revenue growth, though earnings estimate revisions have been modest. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and a C valuation grade indicating fair pricing relative to peers, the stock is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

articles.title: Walmart Inc. (WMT) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
articles.summary: Walmart has recently attracted investor attention with shares returning +7.1% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's -2.6% decline. The company maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with modest earnings estimate revisions and consistent revenue growth forecasts. However, the stock is trading at a premium valuation relative to peers, receiving a D grade on the Value Style Score.

articles.title: This ETF Has Gained 23% This Year. Is It Still Worth Buying in 2026?
articles.summary: As tech stocks struggle post-election, investors are rotating into defensive sectors like healthcare. The State Street Healthcare Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) has gained 23% in 2026, outperforming the S&P 500's 11% return. Healthcare's inelastic demand makes it attractive during market volatility, though investors should consider dollar-cost averaging given the recent run-up.

articles.title: Is iShares Select Dividend ETF (DVY) a Strong ETF Right Now?
articles.summary: The iShares Select Dividend ETF (DVY) is a smart beta ETF offering broad exposure to large cap value stocks with a 3.29% dividend yield and 0.38% expense ratio. Managed by BlackRock with $23.71 billion in assets, DVY tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Select Dividend Index and has delivered 17.76% returns year-to-date. The fund holds 104 stocks with top positions in Pfizer, Altria, and HP, heavily weighted toward Financials, Utilities, and Consumer Staples sectors.

articles.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Over 35% of Berkshire Hathaway's $359 Billion Portfolio Invested in Just 2 Undeniable Winners
articles.summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor at Berkshire Hathaway, maintains the company's investment philosophy of portfolio concentration. Over 35% ($126.7 billion) of Berkshire's $359 billion portfolio is invested in just two companies: Apple ($78.03 billion) and American Express ($48.67 billion). Despite Apple's premium valuation, Abel views it as a multi-decade compounder, while American Express generates an exceptional 45% yield on cost for Berkshire.

articles.title: 3 Dividend Stocks Built for a Market Priced Like It's 1999
articles.summary: With the S&P 500 trading at valuations similar to 1999 (driven by AI hype instead of the dot-com boom), the article recommends three dividend stocks positioned to weather potential market corrections: AbbVie for healthcare stability, Enterprise Products Partners for consistent cash flow, and JPMorgan Chase to benefit from rising interest rates.

articles.title: China Eastern Airlines Signs 23 Procurement Agreements, Unveils Latest Innovations at 9th CIIE
articles.summary: China Eastern Airlines signed 23 procurement agreements worth $540 million with international suppliers at the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The agreements cover aircraft engines, aviation materials, jet fuel, and in-flight catering. Notable deals include spare-engine procurement with CFM International, aviation materials orders with Collins Aerospace and Honeywell, and cabin upgrades with Boeing and Panasonic Avionics. CEAir also showcased innovations including an autonomous electric baggage tractor and modular hangar construction technology.

articles.title: 1 Reason to Still Avoid Wendy's Stock, Even Though It's 10% Below Its 52-Week High
articles.summary: Wendy's stock should be avoided despite trading 10% below its 52-week high due to persistent market share losses and declining same-store sales. The company has slipped to third place in the U.S. fast-food market behind McDonald's and Burger King, with global comparable sales down 5.2% in Q3 and 6.1% year-to-date. New CEO Bob Wright's turnaround strategy faces an uphill battle as customers continue choosing competitors.

articles.title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Home Depot, Gilead Sciences, TotalEnergies, Key Tronic and iPower
articles.summary: Zacks equity research analysts featured five stocks in their daily blog. Home Depot benefits from digital investments and Pro initiatives but faces subdued discretionary projects. Gilead outperforms with strong HIV franchise but faces intensifying competition. TotalEnergies underperforms due to geopolitical risks despite diversified portfolio. Key Tronic struggles with liquidity and debt but has growth prospects from new wins. iPower faces declining revenues and profitability challenges despite recent restructuring.

articles.title: Better U.S. Bank ETF: State Street's KBE vs. First Trust's FTXO
articles.summary: State Street's KBE and First Trust's FTXO offer different approaches to U.S. banking sector exposure. KBE provides broader diversification across 107 holdings with a lower 0.35% expense ratio and higher 2.2% dividend yield, while FTXO concentrates on 50 large-cap banks with an 8% weighting in top holdings. Over five years, both delivered similar returns (~$1,330 per $1,000 invested), but KBE's lower costs and regional bank focus make it better suited for moderate rate-hike environments, whereas FTXO may outperform if the Fed aggressively raises rates.

articles.title: 3 Warren Buffett Stocks Just Closed at Record Highs. Here's the One I'd Still Buy Now.
articles.summary: Apple, Coca-Cola, and Berkshire Hathaway all hit record highs on November 11, 2026. While all three are quality businesses, the analyst recommends Berkshire Hathaway as the best buy at current levels due to its lower valuation relative to earnings compared to Apple and Coca-Cola, plus the added benefit of owning stakes in both other companies indirectly.

articles.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Nearly $110 Billion Invested in These 2 Tech Stocks
articles.summary: Under new CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway maintains significant positions in Apple ($79.4B) and Alphabet ($30.4B), together comprising over 30% of its stock portfolio. While Apple's stock has surged 28% this year due to disciplined AI spending and strong iPhone sales, Alphabet's stock has declined 8% amid concerns over massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure. Despite near-term headwinds, both companies are considered long-term buys given their competitive advantages and valuations.

articles.title: Qualcomm's $5 Billion Data Center Ramp Puts Execution in Focus Now
articles.summary: Qualcomm is transitioning its data center business from development to commercial revenue, targeting $5 billion in fiscal 2027 sales with over $650 million expected in Q1. The company has secured a major deal with Amazon covering up to $60 billion in potential purchases over 10 years. However, early concentration with two hyperscaler customers, margin pressure, and declining fiscal 2027 EPS projections present execution risks as Qualcomm competes against established rivals like NVIDIA and AMD.

articles.title: Few S&P 500 Stocks Yield Over 5%. Here's My Top Pick to Buy Now.
articles.summary: With Treasury yields rising above 5%, dividend stocks are becoming less attractive. However, UPS stands out as one of only ~20 S&P 500 stocks offering yields over 5% at 5.8%. After stabilizing its business by pivoting away from low-margin Amazon deliveries and securing higher-margin customers, UPS is expected to grow revenue 4% and adjusted EPS 2% in 2026. Trading at 15x adjusted EPS with 16 consecutive years of dividend increases, UPS offers a reliable income play for conservative investors.

articles.title: Best Health & Fitness Stocks to Buy on Strong Market Potential
articles.summary: The global health and wellness market is projected to reach $7.76 trillion by 2035 with a 4.94% CAGR, driven by increased consumer spending on fitness, preventive care, and digital health tools. Major technology companies like Apple and Amazon are expanding health-related offerings, while specialized companies in fitness apparel, wearables, and sports equipment are capitalizing on shifting consumer preferences toward personalized wellness solutions.

articles.title: SpaceX's Expanding Ambitions: ETFs to Play Its Next Growth Phase
articles.summary: SpaceX is diversifying beyond rocket launches into AI infrastructure, satellite communications, and lunar operations. The company secured a spot in NASA's $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services program and signed major cloud services deals with Anthropic ($1.25B/month) and Google ($920M/month). Q3 2026 results showed 161% revenue growth to $14.6B with $4.4B net income. Three space-focused ETFs offer significant SpaceX exposure.

articles.title: atQor Named Finalist for 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year Award in - Agents
articles.summary: atQor has been named a finalist for the 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year Award in the Agents category, recognized for its repeatable agentic AI framework and enterprise deployments across nine industries. During FY26, the company developed 252 AI agents with 52 deployed to production environments, delivering measurable business outcomes including 60-70% reduction in manual effort and 50% faster reconciliation in manufacturing finance operations.
